jobs.occupation: Doctoral position in RNA-based crop protection in wheat and potato
jobs.description:
Department of Plant Breeding
Third-cycle subject area
Biology
RNA-based approaches offer new possibilities for protecting crops against disease. Spray-induced gene silencing (SIGS) uses externally applied double-stranded RNA to reduce the expression of selected pathogen genes. Its effectiveness depends on how RNA reaches the pathogen, is taken up and remains biologically active. Understanding these processes is an important step towards reliable RNA-based crop protection.
We are looking for a doctoral student to develop and evaluate SIGS against Septoria tritici blotch in wheat, caused by the fungus Zymoseptoria tritici, and to build on our ongoing research on potato late blight, caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans.
About the position
Establishing SIGS in wheat will be a central part of the project. You will evaluate RNA-based treatments and investigate their effects on pathogen gene expression and disease development. In potato, you will build on established approaches to further investigate RNA-based disease control. Across the two systems, you will also study aspects of RNA uptake, movement and biological activity to better understand the factors that influence treatment effectiveness. The results will help guide the next stages of the project.
The work will combine plant–pathogen experiments, molecular biology, RNA analysis, gene expression studies and microscopy. Depending on the research questions, it may also include small RNA sequencing and bioinformatic analysis. You will receive training in the methods needed for your project and work closely with colleagues in RNA biology and plant pathology.
Your work will combine questions about how RNA functions with the development of new approaches to crop disease control. During your doctoral studies, you will develop your own scientific questions, analyse and publish your results, and present your work at scientific meetings. You will also participate in doctoral courses, seminars and collaboration within and beyond SLU.
Requirements
To meet the general entry requirements you must have been awarded a second-cycle (Master’s) qualification, satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second-cycle, or acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad (Higher Education Ordinance 1993:100, Chapter 7, Section 39).
Specific entry requirements for the third-cycle courses and study programme in Biology. To meet the specific entry requirements, you must hold, or be in the process of completing, a Master’s degree or equivalent in biology, biotechnology, plant breeding, horticulture, agronomy or a related subject, with a relevant focus such as molecular biology, plant pathology, microbiology or plant protection. You must meet the requirements for admission to doctoral education before admission.
You must also meet the equivalent English language requirements as those necessary for the Swedish upper-secondary qualification Engelska B/6.
Your profile
Practical laboratory experience in molecular biology, RNA analysis or plant–microbe interactions is an advantage. Experience with plant disease experiments, fungal or oomycete pathogens, microscopy or bioinformatic analysis of sequencing data is also valuable. You are not expected to have experience in all these areas.
We are looking for someone who is curious, works carefully and takes initiative. You should be able to organise your work, assess results critically and collaborate with others. Good written and spoken English is required. Teaching and supervision of students may be included in the position.
About us
The Department of Plant Breeding at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) conducts research and education to support sustainable production of food, feed and plant-based industrial products. Our research spans plant genetic diversity, genomics, biotechnology, crop improvement, product quality and interactions between plants and their environment. We combine fundamental and applied research to understand important plant traits and develop improved crops and sustainable production methods. Read more about our department here https://www.slu.se/en/about-slu/organisation/departments/vf_en/
This doctoral position is within the subject area Plants and the Environment, where we study crop responses to environmental conditions, disease resistance, RNA biology and interactions between plants and microorganisms. The research includes RNA-based approaches to crop protection and the role of beneficial microorganisms in plant health.

Read more about third-cycle courses and study programmes on http://www.slu.se/utbildning/program-kurser/forskarutbildning/

Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company serving approximately 12 million customers and employing around 21,000 people. We believe there is a way to build a future where everyone can choose fossil-free ways to move, make, and live.

Job Description

Are you a student looking to apply your knowledge to real-world solutions that support the energy transition? With us, you will have the opportunity to complete your thesis project close to the business, working alongside experienced specialists and tackling challenges where your ideas and perspectives can make a real difference.
About the Thesis Work
The Thesis will be held under Corporate Security & Resilience function at Vattenfall which is a modern, flexible, and agile unit that is operating in a challenging and rapidly changing environment. We strive to embed security & resilience into all our business operations and we apply a holistic and risk-based approach to constantly adopt and improve our security posture.
Background and Scope
Cybersecurity exercises, including tabletop exercises and functional exercises are an important part of organizational resilience, particularly for critical infrastructure operators where information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) environments are interconnected. The effectiveness of such exercises depends on the realism, technical accuracy, and relevance of the scenario and its supporting injects (alerts, emails, media reports, decision points).
However, developing scenarios and injects is often manual and resource intensive activity. Exercise planners must translate and combine multiple variables into a sequence that is credible for both IT and OT participants. Generative AI and large language models can support on scenario development, structured content generation and role-based dialogues, while agentic capabilities can enable more adaptive exercises by proposing subsequent injects.
The thesis will investigate how generative AI can support both the design and adaptive facilitation of IT/OT cybersecurity exercises. The thesis will follow a qualitative approach, focusing on the development of a conceptual framework and workflow specification for AI assisted exercise design. The proposed framework and workflow will be evaluated through expert review and walkthroughs with focus on real world applicability and relevance for IT/OT cybersecurity environments.
The thesis is expected to deliver: 
An academic framework for generative AI assisted scenarios and injection design;
A small library of reviewed example artifacts demonstrating the framework;
A documented workflow covering source preparation, scenario generation, state tracking, adaptive inject selection, human approval and debrief support.
A limited demonstrator or simulation showing how participant decisions can change subsequent injects and scenario outcomes.
Output and summary of experts after review where they will analyze the risk factors and the possible adoption issue that they foresee.

This thesis project is for 2 students.

Qualifications

We are looking for students who are about to complete their academic studies and are eager to apply their knowledge in a real-world setting through a thesis project at Vattenfall. You are someone who shares our values and identifies with our principles: Active, Open, Positive and Safety.

jobs.description:
Join Telavox as a Systems Engineer for Storage
Are you a hands-on systems engineer who thrives in operational depth and wants to own the storage that the rest of engineering runs on? At Telavox, we run our own: our own Ceph clusters, on-prem Kubernetes, and a fleet of physical servers across six countries. We're providers of infrastructure, not consumers of cloud - a deliberate choice, and what our product and economics demand. Storage is where we're investing next.
Ceph specifically is not a requirement. If you've run distributed or enterprise storage in production - Ceph, ZFS, Gluster, Lustre, MinIO, a vendor array - the instincts are what we're after, and we'll teach you ours.
About the job
This is a hands-on operations role. You'd own how our storage runs day-to-day - health, capacity, upgrades, expansion, and the operational foundations underneath it. You'll have real input into architecture, and you'll set the long-term direction with our storage lead rather than on your own. The emphasis here is deliberately operational - if making storage actually work, and being trusted to do it unsupervised, is the part you want, there's a lot of room in this role.
Ceph (block and S3) is our main estate - real production storage, growing across regions, with Sweden the largest footprint.
Your day-to-day would be mostly spent on things like:

Keeping the clusters healthy - issues, monitoring, capacity planning, upgrades, and expansion across regions

Getting the foundations right: stability, security, predictable scaling.

Making the work repeatable - runbooks, upgrade procedures that hold across regions, automation for what's manual today

You won't work in isolation from the rest of the platform: on-prem Kubernetes runs most of our workloads and has clear impact on the storage domain, and our Ansible-driven server and OS fleet spans six countries

How we work together:
You’ll join our Infrastructure Engineering team of around 15 people, working from our Malmö HQ, Gjuteriet, with international colleagues working remotely. English is our working language, and Swedish is a bonus.
There’s no mandatory on-call rotation, although Compute and Storage have an informal secondary list. You’ll have real ownership from day one, with plenty of room to identify, propose, and implement improvements. We also use Claude Code across Engineering, and you’ll help explore how it can support our platform work.
About you
You treat automation as the direction and repetition as its trigger, you factor in risk from the start rather than discovering it at the end, and you're pragmatic enough to do the manual work until automation catches up.
We're looking for:

Real operational depth in distributed or enterprise storage - a system you've run in production, been on the hook for, and debugged under pressure. Which system matters far less than how deeply

Strong Linux fundamentals - the substrate everything else sits on

Comfort taking an unclear problem, scoping it, and seeing it through

We strongly value experience with Ceph or object storage at scale, Ansible or similar configuration management, and operating systems across distributed environments. Experience with on-prem Kubernetes, server/OS lifecycle management, or firmware, BIOS, and BMC/IPMI is also a plus.
We’re looking for someone at a mid-to-senior level, with growth focused on deeper expertise, broader ownership, and becoming the go-to person for storage across the organisation.
Join us at Telavox 💚
Since Telavox's journey started in 2002, we have strengthened our position as the leading forward-thinking communication platform for businesses. As a digital mobile operator, we develop and own our all-in-one communication platform, which integrates telephony, PBX, messaging, meetings, and contact centers, giving businesses a smarter way to connect.
Today, we’re a thriving company with 1.9 billion SEK in revenue and 500+ Telavoxers across nine countries. We embrace AI and automation to push the boundaries of business communication.
We offer flexible work options and adaptable hours, giving you the freedom to balance life and career while staying connected to our vibrant Telavox culture.

At Telavox, we don't focus on fitting in; we focus on making room for everyone.

Own and improve the batch layer on GCP, working with BigQuery, Airflow, and dbt to deliver reliable, well-modelled, and cost-efficient pipelines.

Design and ship customer-facing backend services
Design, build, and operate backend APIs that customers use directly, with strong attention to contracts, versioning, performance, and backwards compatibility.
Think through failure modes, observability, and scaling up front, so services behave predictably in production.

Improve how we structure infrastructure code through reusable modules, sensible environment separation, and safe, repeatable deployments.
Drive improvements in monitoring, alerting, security, and cost visibility across clouds. Participate in a shared on-call rotation for production systems.

Lead technical design discussions and write clear design documents for significant changes, bringing the team along in the reasoning.
Identify technical debt and architectural weak points and build a pragmatic plan to address them alongside feature work.

Lead and mentor

Mentor two junior engineers through pairing, thoughtful code reviews, and gradually increasing ownership, helping them grow into confident, independent engineers.

REQUIREMENTS 
Significant professional experience as a software or data engineer (typically 6+ years), including time spent owning production systems end to end.
Strong software engineering fundamentals: clean and modular design, testing strategies, API design, and an understanding of distributed systems trade-offs.
Experience building and operating backend services in a compiled or typed language such as Go, Java, Kotlin, Rust, or similar.

Solid experience with infrastructure as code using Terraform, and working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider in depth.

A track record of mentoring others and raising the quality of the teams you've been part of.
Clear written and verbal communication, especially the ability to explain technical decisions and trade-offs to engineers of varying experience.

Professional experience with Go. This is a strong plus, though we'll happily support an experienced backend engineer in going deep on it.
Experience running infrastructure across multiple clouds and regions, including networking, identity, and data residency considerations.
Background with lambda or kappa architectures, event streaming systems (such as Kafka or Pub/Sub), or high-throughput API gateways.
Experience with observability tooling (metrics, tracing, logging) and cloud cost optimization.

Hos oss blir du del av en engagerad och varm arbetsgemenskap där glädje, professionalism och samarbete går hand i hand. Du får chansen att göra verklig skillnad för elever – samtidigt som du får utvecklas i ditt yrke.

Skicka in din ansökan och bli en del av vårt fantastiska team!

Internationella Engelska Skolan (IES) is a leading independent school group with academic results far above average and a diverse and energetic staff. Teaching is in both Swedish and English, and the hallways are bilingual. The language of meetings and communication amongst the staff is English.

IES is one of Sweden's largest school groups at compulsory school level with 46 schools and around 30,000 students across the country. IES has grown steadily and maintained quality since 1993.

Responsibilities: 
Follow up proactive health and safety measures across the factory 

Conduct or coordinate different types of HSE testing 

Develop and deliver safety training 

Follow up employees, managers, and cases in the IA system 

Support and guide managers regarding deviations 

Participate in or lead incident investigations of varying scope

Bachelor's degree in HSE engineering, preparedness and crisis management, occupational hygiene, or another closely relevant field

We think you are a forward thinker and a team thriver, who is naturally curious, and solutions oriented. You communicate with honesty and respect, are eager to take initiative and dedicated to follow through. Above all, you are ready to take responsibility and grow as an expert.

You hold a relevant university degree completed in 2025 or later. You can communicate clearly in English, hold a valid driver’s license and are available to start in September 2027.
